Definition: from G575 and G1218; absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller:--taking a far journey.
BiblicalUsage: Once, about the Son of man as a man taking a far journey — He left His house, gave authority to His servants and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.
TheologicalSignificance: One parable, one command: the Master is away, the work is assigned, and the porter watches.
